mainEntity.name: What should I do immediately after clicking an AI-generated phishing link?

acceptedAnswer.mainText:
Act fast, the sooner you respond, the better your chances of stopping damage.

  * **Disconnect from suspicious websites immediately** and close the browser tab without entering more information.
  * **Change affected passwords right away**, especially if you reused them across accounts.
  * **Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA)** on banking, email, and social media accounts.
  * **Run a browser security scan** to detect malicious extensions, downloads, or hidden threats.

If you’re unsure what to do next, Guardio explains the recovery steps in [what to do if you click on a phishing link.](https://guard.io/blog/what-to-do-if-you-click-on-a-phishing-link)
acceptedAnswer.name: Why are AI scam emails suddenly so much more believable?

acceptedAnswer.mainText:
Because scammers now use AI to mimic writing styles, personal details, and even workplace language patterns.

  * **Watch for urgency tactics** like “act now,” “payment failed,” or “account suspended.”
  * **Double-check sender domains carefully** since AI scams often spoof trusted companies with tiny spelling changes.
  * **Be cautious with personalized messages** that reference your workplace, hobbies, or recent activity.
  * **Avoid opening unexpected attachments** even if the email sounds professional or familiar.

Learn how modern phishing works in Guardio’s breakdown of [phishing scams explained.](https://guard.io/blog/phishing-explained-everything-you-need-to-know-about-phishing-scams)
acceptedAnswer.name: Can deepfake videos be used to scam employees at work?

acceptedAnswer.mainText:
Yes, scammers increasingly use fake executive videos and AI-generated meeting calls to pressure employees into sending money or sharing data.

  * **Verify unusual financial requests** through a second communication channel like Slack or a direct phone call.
  * **Train teams to spot deepfake glitches** such as awkward blinking, delayed lip sync, or robotic facial movement.
  * **Restrict approval authority** so large payments require multiple people to confirm.
  * **Be skeptical of “urgent confidentiality” requests** designed to stop employees from asking questions.

Businesses can strengthen defenses with Guardio’s advice on [cyber security for small businesses.](https://guard.io/blog/cyber-security-for-small-businesses)

pages.title: Indirect Prompt Injection: A New Security Threat in AI Systems
pages.text: Indirect prompt injection is a new security threat in AI systems that can compromise the integrity of AI models and lead to unintended behavior. This threat is particularly concerning because it can be difficult to detect and mitigate, as it often involves subtle manipulation of AI prompts and inputs. In this article, we will explore the risks and consequences of indirect prompt injection and provide guidance on how to mitigate this threat.

pages.title: The dangers of AI agents unfurling hyperlinks and what to do about it
pages.summary: Unfurling refers to an application expanding (retrieving) a hyperlink automatically to show us a preview of the page. This can lead to data exfiltration and is a threat in LLM (large language model) powered Chatbots and Slack Apps. To mitigate this threat, Slack Apps can disable unfurling by setting the "unfurl_links" field to False in the message JSON object.
